//: The RAM32 DFFRAM macro (macros/, the AND-OR read path built in DFFRAM.librelane models/ram_ao, 320.16 x 116.96) instead of the synthesized src/RAM32.v: on the core's bottom row at the right (x 349.83 = 9 x 38.87, the tile's stripe pitch, so its power pin columns lie on tile stripes; y 2.72, the row grid), halos 2 x 1 um (the macro keeps its own 2.72 / 1.38 um margins; cut_rows cuts the row overlapping the halo, a touching one survives) and FP_PRUNE_THRESHOLD dropping the 17-site row stubs between the macro and the core edge that pdngen could not power (PDN-0179; RESPIN.md, the halo trial). The tile's stripes are run over its met4 power pins by flow.py's Tile.ExtendPowerStripes, so pdngen's own connectivity check is not the verdict; src/RAM32.v stays as a model for lint (EXTRA_VERILOG_MODELS), the macro's netlist has no power pins

GPL_CELL_PADDING 2 (a site each side of every cell in global placement, +35% on this design's 2.6 um average cell) reserves the room the flow fills afterwards: the std cells are 60% of the rows after placement and the slew/fanout repair (+16%, 2598 buffers), CTS (+4%) and the 1400 hold buffers (+10%) then took the densest 30 um bins to 92-100%, where the detailed router did not converge (density 85 and 68 alike: 48 and 46 bins over 90%). With the padding the placer's utilization is 81%, so the target density goes back up to 85 (81% of a bin in padded cells is 63% in real ones). TT07 placed at 77 on the 8x2 tile.

MAX_FANOUT_CONSTRAINT 16 and PL_RESIZER_HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN 0.07 (2026-10-17, the streaming-fetch RTL): with the design 3% bigger than rc1 the padded placement was at its density limit and every draw packed a corner to 90% where the router stalled (12K violations after 12 iterations free, 1 stuck after 56 anchored). Fanout 16 halves the fanout violations (146 -> 35) but gives no area back (repair_design upsizes the drivers instead of buffering); the hold margin does: 0.1 -> 0.07 ns takes 1346 hold buffers to 591 (the flop-to-flop paths sit in a 50-100 ps band of raw hold slack at the fast corner, ~400 buffers per 10 ps), 7.4k um2 of standard cells, and the corners back to rc1's 71-77%; it routed clean in 12 iterations (runs/macro-stream-fo16-hold07: hold ws 0.077 ns at ff against rc1's 0.109, setup +5.5 ns nominal / -7.2 at ss, Magic DRC / LVS / antenna 0). 0.05 ns (191 buffers, hold ws 0.056) routed as well; Ken chose 0.07. Both measured first with TO=OpenROAD.GlobalRouting (trial_fanout16*.json).

PDN_CFG: LibreLane's PDN plus a met4 stripe (with pdngen's vias to the rails) on each macro power pin column that is not on a tile stripe; Tile.ExtendPowerStripes then runs the columns over the macro.

ANCHOR_CELLS_TABLE: the placement replayed from the release candidate, rc3 (placements/macro-rc3_final_cells.json, an odb_anchor_cells.py --dump of runs/macro-rc3's final ODB, 2026-10-18; itself a draw anchored to rc2's table): the registers matched by RTL name and the logic by structure, so a rebuild of the same netlist reproduces this placement and a rebuild after an RTL change reuses what still matches (rc3 matched 5354 cells of rc2's table, 317 registers new or renamed, and routed clean; after the streaming fetch the ao5 table matched 6448 cells and routed to 1 stuck violation - a changed design is a new draw, judge it at global routing). rc2's table is kept as an option: make macro OVERLAY=trial_anchor_rc2.json; a free draw: OVERLAY=trial_anchor_free.json.
//art: The chip art (art/calvin, chip_art.py 2026-10-18, Ken's calvin from prism's hand-edited cell): met4 only, 32.4 x 47.4 um, on bare oxide as in prism (Ken: that is what makes it visible): Project.ArtKeepout cuts the rows under the box and ROUTING_OBSTRUCTIONS keeps the router off it on met1-met4, Project.ChipArt merges the cell into the GDS after stream-out and adds the box to the LEF. The box is the upper-right corner, in the channel between the last PDN stripe pair (x 641/644) and the right edge's stripe (679.9): Ken's choice - in a corner nothing routes around the keep-out, the cells just move inward - and the best of three free-draw trials to the global route (corner 1.133M um of wire, met3 41.4% / overflow 3; mid right edge 1.151M, 45.4% / 9; a met4-only box in the centre 1.139M).
